version.changelog: Initial release: public one-shot download links via Cloudflare Tunnel, configurable TTL, auto-cleanup

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: share-onetime-link
Version: 1.0.0

The skill facilitates sharing local files over the public internet by deploying a local Express server and exposing it via a Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared). While the code in server.js and share-file.js implements several security best practices—including cryptographically random tokens, one-time-use download logic, and path sanitization (path.basename) to prevent directory traversal—the inherent nature of creating a public tunnel to a local environment is a high-risk capability that bypasses traditional firewall boundaries. There is no evidence of intentional malice, but the architectural requirement to expose local ports to the internet warrants a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (serves one-time links via a local Express server + Cloudflare Tunnel) but has operational mismatches and an exposure/privacy risk (a publicly reachable /status endpoint that can leak filenames and token metadata) and minor metadata mismatches.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with the code and required binaries: node is required to run the server and cloudflared is required to expose it. Asking for cloudflared makes sense for public exposure. Minor mismatch: registry lists no required env vars but SKILL.md and the code expect SHARE_PUBLIC_URL (and optionally SHARE_PORT/SHARED_DIR).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and server code expose three public endpoints: POST /generate, GET /dl/:token, and GET /status. When the user follows SKILL.md and runs a Cloudflare Tunnel to localhost:5050, all endpoints (including /status) will be reachable via the public hostname. /status returns filenames and truncated token prefixes, and /generate will allow anyone who can reach the tunnel to create tokens for files in the shared/ directory — there is no authentication or IP restriction described. This is an operational exposure/privacy issue that may be unexpected to users.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote, opaque download is used; the skill includes source files and uses npm-installed dependencies (express) from the public registry. The install instructions require running npm install locally and running cloudflared. This is relatively low risk compared with arbitrary binary downloads, but the included code will run an HTTP server and should be reviewed before starting.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata declares no required env vars, but SKILL.md and the code expect SHARE_PUBLIC_URL (and optionally SHARE_PORT and SHARED_DIR). The skill does not request any unrelated credentials, and it does not read other system credentials, so privilege scope is limited — however the missing declared env vars is a metadata inconsistency the user should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated platform privileges. It does not modify other skills or system-wide configs. It runs as a normal user process when started.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill implements a legitimate one-time-link server, but review and operationalize it carefully before use:

- Understand public exposure: running cloudflared as documented will expose every route (including /status and /generate) to the public hostname. /status discloses filenames and token metadata; /generate lets an unauthenticated caller create download tokens for any file present in the shared/ folder. If you will expose the tunnel publicly, restrict access (Cloudflare Access/Zero Trust, IP allowlists, or remove /status) or add authentication.

- Avoid putting sensitive files into the SHARED_DIR. Only copy files you intend to share. By default SHARED_DIR is workspace/shared/ unless you override it.

- Consider removing or hardening the /status endpoint and adding authentication or an allowlist to /generate if you want stronger privacy guarantees.

- Metadata mismatch: the registry says no required env vars but SKILL.md and the scripts use SHARE_PUBLIC_URL, SHARE_PORT, and SHARED_DIR — set these deliberately and ensure the public URL matches a tunnel binding.

- Run the server in an isolated environment (container or dedicated machine) and inspect the included files (they are small and readable) before starting. If you need strict security guarantees, consider adding TLS/auth at the tunnel level or modifying the code to require a secret for /generate and /status.

If you accept these operational caveats and harden the exposure (or only run the tunnel for short-lived sessions), the skill's behavior is coherent with its stated purpose. If you plan to expose it permanently or to share sensitive files, treat it as risky until you add authentication and restrict the tunnel.
